newsitem.title: GERMANY: SKW Trostberg eyes dividend rise after sales jump.
newsitem.headline: SKW Trostberg eyes dividend rise after sales jump.

text.p: German chemicals group SKW Trostberg AG on Wednesday reported a four percent rise in nine-month sales, putting it in line to meet full-year results forecasts and raise its 1996 dividend by 10 percent.

"The year 1996 will be a good one for SKW Trostberg both in terms of sales and profits," chief executive Wilhelm Simson told a news conference, promising strong results should translate into a 1.10 mark (73 cents) per share dividend payout.
During the first nine months of the year, group sales climbed to 2.97 billion marks, fuelled largely by higher fertiliser sales and particularly strong turnover in North America, Simson said.
Operating profit, for which the company declined to give precise figures, was at high year-ago levels.

The results, previewed two weeks ago when SKW Trostberg's majority shareholder VIAG AG released its own nine-month data, were slightly below analyst expectations but did not erase management forecasts that 1996 profits will climb 10 percent.

While full year sales, seen at 3.9 billion marks, and operating profit, expected around 280 million marks, will be mostly flat, lower tax payments will help boost pre-tax profits, delivering the forecast 10 percent profit increase.
Group net profit is forecast to be up 21 percent at 145 million marks, Simson added.

In 1997, when this year's takeover of construction chemicals group Master Builders Technologies (MBT) from Swiss group Sandoz AG will impact results, "profits will rise more strongly than sales," chief financial officer Klaus-Juergen Schulz added.

The group, which became the world's biggest construction chemicals group with the MBT takeover, concentrates on three business areas, natural food stuffs, specialty chemicals and construction chemicals.

Although MBT's 1.3 billion Swiss franc price tag will weigh on net profits next year, Schulz said earnings per share will surely be above this year's levels which he said will be at least 2.20 marks. Analysts predicted 1997 earnings per share to be around 2.90 marks.

"For me the SKW Trostberg story is still intact," said Kleinwort Benson analyst Lutz Grueten, adding shares, which took a beating in recent days, should recover as the company promises long-term steady growth.

Although SKW Trostberg, a favourite with investors since it floated shares last year, presented a stunning 66 percent profit jump last year, the group said it preferred delivering steady, step-by-step growth.

For the moment, SKW Trostberg, fresh from an aggressive buying spree which brought in Systems Bio-Industries from French group Sanofi SA in 1994 and now MBT, said it needs to focus on digesting its takeovers, which jump-started growth.
"In 1997 we expect to grow internally," Simson said, adding that the group's debt, swelling to two billion marks after the MBT acquisition, "will likely prevent a spectacular takeover."

Investors were relieved to hear SKW Trostberg currently sees no need to raise capital to pay for MBT deciding instead that bank loans, in yen, dollars, mark and Swiss francs, will in the long run be a cheaper financing method.
SKW Trostberg shares closed Frankfurt bourse trade up 1.49 marks at 42.89 marks.
